designationHistory.name: Sully's Hill Park
designationHistory.indexText: President Theodore Roosevelt reserved the land as Sully's Hill Park by Proclamation 530 on June 2, 1904, under the act ratifying the Devils Lake Reservation land agreement.

sources.name: U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service: White Horse Hill National Game Preserve, About Us

American Presidency Project: Proclamation 530, June 2, 1904 (Theodore Roosevelt), reserving lands "for public use as a park to be known as Sully's Hill Park" under the act ratifying the Devils Lake agreement
Wikisource: Executive Order 3596, Dec. 22, 1921, also making the "Sullys Hill National Park Game Preserve" a bird refuge

review.by: Accepted on the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service's own record (Library decision)
